Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: Lpg consumption in sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (mt), compared to 2.9 mt during the same month a year earlier. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in july. Erratic monsoon conditions due to el nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.

Article Title: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags gets major green upgrade with 20.8 million kWh solar project amid lawsuits
Article Text:
​Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Six Flags Magic Mountain solar project now powers two parks

Travis Kelce’s Six Flags endorsement adds another spotlight

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A theme park parking lot is usually a place where cars sit before the real fun begins. At Six Flags Magic Mountain in California, it now plays a much bigger role. The park has fully activated a major solar power project covering thousands of parking spaces, turning an everyday guest facility into a large-scale energy source. The installation is designed to generate enough electricity to offset the annual consumption of both Six Flags Magic Mountain and neighbouring Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles. The move also arrives as NFL star Travis Kelce continues his high-profile relationship with Six Flags as the company’s brand ambassador.The newly energised project includes solar canopies covering 4,315 parking spaces, giving the Magic Mountain parking area a striking new purpose. The system has a 12.37-megawatt solar capacity, making it the largest solar carport installation in California, according to project information.The solar installation is expected to produce around 20.8 million kWh of electricity each year. Six Flags says that output is equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of Magic Mountain and Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles combined.The project also features an 8 MWh battery energy storage system and 109 electric vehicle charging stations.That means the development is not simply about putting solar panels above cars. It combines power generation, energy storage and EV infrastructure in one large site.The project had been announced earlier, but its full commissioning marks the key milestone. The solar canopies cover roughly 637,000 square feet, with 22,908 solar modules spread across 36 long-span carport structures.The message shown in the accompanying Parks & Loisirs post sums up the scale of the development: “Le parking de Six Flags Magic Mountain alimente désormais deux parcs en énergie solaire.” Translated, it means the Six Flags Magic Mountain parking lot now supplies solar energy to two parks.The image also states that the 12.37 MW installation covers 4,315 parking spaces and that its yearly production should match the combined electricity consumption of Magic Mountain and Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles.The sustainability push comes during a major branding chapter for Six Flags. In March 2026, the company announced Travis Kelce as a brand ambassador for 2026. His role includes digital content, social media campaigns and approved use of his name, image and likeness across broadcast, streaming and in-park marketing.Kelce has also described himself as a lifelong Six Flags fan. In the company's announcement, he said:“Six Flags parks were a hallmark of my childhood and the scene of some of my most fun and cherished memories, and I’m excited to team up with the company as it enters its next chapter. The Six Flags team is creating even more rides and attractions as it takes guest engagement to a new level. I look forward to helping them continue to build excitement for their unrivaled portfolio of parks and introduce a new generation of fans to unforgettable experiences. ”His endorsement gives Six Flags a familiar sports personality while the company makes changes beyond rides and attractions. At Magic Mountain, the parking lot itself has become part of that next chapter, producing renewable energy on a scale capable of supporting two major Southern California parks.
Article Summary: Six flags magic mountain solar project now powers two parks. The park has fully activated a major solar power project covering thousands of parking spaces. The installation is designed to generate enough electricity to offset the annual consumption of both parks.

Article Title: LeBron James’ wife Savannah James’ latest flight incident offers an important rich-people financial lesson as the internet argues over dopamine-hitting morality
Article Text:
Savannah James and her bestie, April McDaniel. Image via: JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images

Savannah James and April McDaniel on their flight arrangement

Critics and defenders split over the seat gap

Savannah and McDaniel respond to the backlash

The money lesson inside the seat split

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It’s not easy to be rich. While LeBron James has built his massive financial empire from his career earnings, several business ventures, and endorsements, his wife, Savannah James, is slowly climbing the ladder to create her own financial empire. Recently, news of Savannah and her best friend, April McDaniel, broke online. Fans were quite upset, most of them anyway, and the reason for their big upset was that dopamine-hitting morality was missing from the picture. The two laid out the arrangement on the Sept. 28 episode of Boardroom's Mental Wealth podcast, and the clip has been fought over online ever since.But that was the point, McDaniel was not upset, and her account secretly revealed an important lesson. Let’s have a look at what happened first and how their reactions to the incident gave away a subtle message about money.The hosts, Rich Kleiman and Jack Howard, opened with a broad question about how friendship and money mix, and the exchange came about four minutes into the episode. McDaniel answered first. She said the two live different lifestyles and neither pretends otherwise.It shows in how they travel. McDaniel can't take a spontaneous trip, so the pair book well ahead, which keeps costs down, and James leaves enough time for McDaniel to get her finances lined up.They don't turn up at Fashion Week on a week's notice, whatever people assume about how they move. On a recent trip, reportedly to Japan according to local media, James took first class and McDaniel took business. First was outside what McDaniel planned to spend, and she saw no reason to match James seat for seat. They laugh about it, she said.The two are not casual travel companions. They have been friends for well over a decade, and McDaniel described the move into business together as organic. They co-host the podcast Everybody's Crazy and run a holding company called Signed, and James owns the skincare brand, Reframe Beauty. McDaniel also runs a creative agency.The seat split had come up on their own show before the Mental Wealth appearance, McDaniel said, and some viewers were openly critical. One detail seemed to bother people most. During flights, she goes up front, gets into James' bed and watches a movie with her. “And I was like: ‘Why? I can't afford first,'” April said.The hosts then asked James whether friends had ever expected her to cover a first-class seat for them.Celebrity Net Worth puts Savannah's wealth near $100 million.Critics started with cost. A $10,000 fare is very negligible for Savannah. Others said withholding an upgrade felt like a quiet reminder that the two women are not on the same level. A few wanted James to either buy the ticket or sit in economy with her friend. Some asked why anyone would sit alone on a long flight just to prove a point.Paying with points does not make the seat free, since taxes and fees still have to be paid in cash and can run into the thousands.Commenters argued that paying once invites more, first the spa day and then the dinner check. Boundaries, in this view, are what let a friendship survive a wealth gap, and handouts can breed resentment or entitlement. Praise went to McDaniel for staying within her means and to James for not letting friends become moochers.Former Knicks star Brandon Jennings sided with them on X. His post, from @Tuff__Crowd: "If you can't afford first class or certain things when you around your rich friends and you feel entitled that they should pay, Ur a certified moocher…Savannah James ain't wrong."McDaniel called it ridiculous to assume everybody should fly first and said expectations need managing. She described a recent run-in with someone stunned that she flies commercial instead of private, and she played it for laughs by asking the person if they were okay. In her view, social media has bent people's sense of what things cost, and people used to fast money treat it differently than people who earn it slowly. She wants others to know it is fine to live a normal life.Her rule for money is to worry about yourself. The two live in separate worlds, she said, and meet up to talk about them. She credits James with adjusting to where she is financially, and says the friendship runs on feel. If a plan doesn't feel good to both of them, they skip it.James spoke to the other half of the question. Her friends, she said, understand the situation before any trip begins, and every one of them respects it. Nobody has asked her to take care of a cost or be responsible for them. It "has never, ever been that," she said. She voiced gratitude for that understanding.McDaniel stressed that the friendship holds because each side respects the other's finances.On the podcast, two women with very different bank balances said out loud what each can spend, and neither apologized for her number. They didn’t have to.Howard, who leads money wellness at Ally and has taught budgeting for 16 years, shared that she believes a bank account should show a person's values, and for most people it doesn't. She opens with a question about a person's first memory of money, because she sees two common mistakes, people don't know their money story, and they don't know what they value now. Neither is a math problem. Shame does more damage than arithmetic. Someone who can't afford brunch puts it on a card instead of saying so. Her fix is one honest sentence that offers a cheaper plan, because once it is said, "shame loses its power."James described her own version. Her tax bracket and the prices around her have changed, she said, but her view of what things are worth has not. Spending that follows values makes the seat choice easy for both women: McDaniel pays for what fits her plan, and James pays for what fits hers.Of course, the higher earner does not have to match a friend's standard of living, and saying what each person can afford keeps the relationship steady. Experts also advise telling friends honestly how much you can spend before signing up for travel or dinners.Howard offers a practical start for anyone with uneven income. Fold a sheet of paper into three columns and log every expense, the emotion behind it and the value it served. Do it for 30 days, then build next year's budget from what the log shows.
Article Summary: Savannah james and her bestie, april mcdaniel, sat together in first class on a recent flight to japan. The two laid out the arrangement on the sept. 28 episode of boardroom's mental wealth podcast. The clip has been fought over online ever since. Critics and defenders split over the seat gap.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay high court has directed x corp to remove a video against serum institute of india pvt ltd and its ceo adar poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer yohan tengra immediately after its june 5, 2023 order. Justice gauri godse of hc on tuesday passed the order on an interim application in the pending defamation suit.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: Factory growth hits 7-month high, pmi rises to 55.1. Stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since may, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses. Revenues reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments. European technology shares rose 2.4% and the us chip index gained 1.5%.

Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus on how Steve Jobs’ ‘furniture story’ inspires product design at the company
Article Text:
The ‘carpenter's lesson’

Apple CEO John Ternus, who recently stepped into the top leadership position after guiding the company’s hardware engineering teams across multiple device generations, has shared how an iconic Steve Jobs philosophy continues to dictate Apple ’s design standards – even on its most budget-friendly devices. Speaking soon after the launch of the MacBook Neo earlier this year, Ternus revisited one of his favourite stories about the late Apple co-founder, illustrating how attention to unseen details remains the foundation of the company’s product line.Ternus recounted a quiet moment involving Jobs moving a bedroom dresser away from the wall.“Steve was moving a piece of furniture, a chest of drawers, and pulled it away from the wall and looked at the back and was just reflecting on the carpenter who had made it beautiful. It finished the back as beautifully as the rest of it, even though nobody was going to see it right and I think about that all the time because I think that perfectly exemplifies what we do here,” he said.The mindset of treating internal components and unseen surfaces with the same engineering precision as the exterior casing has been a foundational rule of Apple hardware since the earliest Macintosh models. Ternus connected that design ethos directly to the MacBook Neo, pointing out that cost-effective pricing does not mean cutting corners on aesthetic or structural integrity.“We've been talking about the MacBook Neo. Here is our most affordable Mac we've ever made, and it's absolutely beautiful. And if you open it up and look inside, it's just as beautiful,” Tetanus said.“And that's true about all products – an iPhone Pro Max or a MacBook Pro or an iPad Pro, but it's also true on a MacBook Neo,” he added, suggesting that Apple applies the exact same standards to its entry-level hardware.For Ternus, continuing to obsess over hidden details provides a clear roadmap for where the company is headed under his tenure.“That's what we do, and so, it's just been really good just to think about that and reflect on that because that is probably the best kind of clue as to where we're going in the future. We're going to keep pushing in that same way,” Ternus said.
Article Summary: Apple ceo john ternus has shared how an iconic steve jobs philosophy continues to dictate apple’s design standards. He recounted a quiet moment involving jobs moving a bedroom dresser away from the wall. ‘steve was moving a piece of furniture, a chest of drawers, and looked at the back and was just reflecting on the carpenter who had made it beautiful,’ he said.

Article Title: As Elon Musk plans to shake up mobile industry, AT&T CEO John Stankey says that the economics and technical aspects of Starlink's plan don't line up
Article Text:
Starlink aims to challenge telecom operators

AT&T's counter-bet: fiber over satellite

Starlink's mobile ambitions

The cost problem

Why Stankey says the math doesn't work

Analysts remain skeptical too

AT&T CEO John Stankey has cast doubt on Musk's plans to turn SpaceX's Starlink satellite network into a direct competitor to wireless carriers, arguing that the economics and technical realities behind the strategy do not add up. Speaking to Axios, Stankey described SpaceX's ambition of becoming a major challenger to traditional telecom companies as "not a viable strategy," even as Elon Musk and Gwynne Shotwell, president of SpaceX, have outlined plans to expand Starlink beyond satellite internet and into mobile services.The comments come as SpaceX seeks to leverage Starlink's growing satellite network to compete more directly with established telecom operators. Shotwell recently said she expects Starlink to win customers from traditional carriers, arguing that the company's service would be superior. The remarks rattled investors, with shares of major telecom firms including AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile reportedly falling after SpaceX highlighted its ambitions. According to SpaceX's public disclosures, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and a constellation of 10,200 satellites covering 167 countries as of June 30.The connectivity business accounted for 55% of SpaceX's revenue, making it the company's biggest revenue generator.AT&T is leaning hard on fiber infrastructure to grow its internet business at a moment when AI is driving surging demand for connectivity. The company announced a $3 billion deal with Corning on Tuesday to expand that infrastructure, arguing fiber delivers speeds three times faster than satellite. Stankey was blunt about the comparison, telling Axios that nothing beats fiber, and that even if satellite technology performs at its absolute best over the next decade, it still won't be able to match what fiber delivers.Starlink already competes with traditional telecom companies for home and business internet customers, and SpaceX has now started talking openly about a mobile business that would put it in direct competition with wireless carriers. Shotwell added fuel to that narrative in August, during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company, predicting the company would win over a meaningful number of customers because its service would simply be better. That comment sent shares of AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile falling the following day.As of June 30, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and more than 10,200 satellites providing coverage across 167 countries. While SpaceX's rockets and AI work tend to dominate headlines, its connectivity business is actually its largest revenue driver, accounting for 55% of total sales.Becoming a genuine fourth major US mobile carrier would require significantly more terrestrial infrastructure to match a traditional cellular network's capacity — a build-out one analyst estimated could cost SpaceX more than $100 billion. SpaceX's alternative: installing small cellular base stations alongside Starlink dishes at homes and businesses, adding ground-based capacity where satellite alone falls short, without building a sprawling cell tower network. Musk claims these stations could eventually deliver connectivity directly to phones with better and higher bandwidth than existing carriers offer.Stankey argued that installing enough small stations to match a traditional network's capacity would cost roughly the same as building a full macro cellular network. He also flagged a regulatory hurdle: current law doesn't allow radiating cellular signals from someone's home without their permission, unless the law changes. If the approach were genuinely viable, he argued, AT&T would already be doing it on its own fiber network. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment.Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei wrote that cell towers aren't going anywhere soon, even if Musk gets creative, citing technical hurdles extending satellite coverage indoors, limited brand awareness, and customer reluctance to switch carriers. She suggested Starlink Mobile could fill a meaningful gap in remote, rural, maritime, or disaster scenarios, but remains a long way from replacing terrestrial carrier networks. operators' brands. She said Starlink Mobile could prove valuable in rural, remote, maritime and disaster-response scenarios but remains "a long way" from replacing terrestrial cellular networks.Despite the scepticism, the growing confrontation between SpaceX and established telecom providers highlights how satellite-based connectivity is increasingly moving into territory historically dominated by mobile network operators. As both sides invest billions to shape the future of communications, the battle between fibre, cellular networks and satellite internet appears set to intensify.
Article Summary: At&t ceo john stankey casts doubt on spacex's plans to become a direct competitor to wireless carriers. Stankey says the economics and technical realities behind the strategy do not add up. The comments come as spacex seeks to leverage starlink's growing satellite network to compete more directly with established telecom operators.

Article Title: Amazon Web Services' Swami Sivasubramanian says that CEOs are no longer worried if AI will add value to their businesses, now they have a new 'fear'
Article Text:
AI has boosted profits, but the jump is not substantial

The ‘Big AI Question’ seems to have changed. Until 2025, the general artificial intelligence (AI) worry was if investment in the technology was really worth it and if it will add to the bottomline. The same has shifted in 2026, and now the key concern is how safe are AI Agents. Companies do not yet trust AI with important decisions. According to a report by GeekWire, this was the general consensus at the recent Madrona's IA40 Summit. The Madrona's IA40 Summit is the venture capital company's annual gathering of AI startups, investors and tech executives. Zico Kolter, the Carnegie Mellon professor who chairs the safety and security committee of OpenAI's board, said that as of now Companies do not yet trust AI with important decisions. According to Kolter, the ability to control AI systems has to keep pace with their capabilities, which might mean developing them more slowly than is possible.His view was shared by Amazon Web Services (AWS) Agentic AI and Emerging Technologies organization head Swami Sivasubramanian. AWS's top executives said that most CEOs and CTOs worry about whether an AI agent will always follow their company’s rules and regulations.Speaking at the Summit, Sivasubramanian said that nearly every CIO and CEO raises the same question about AI agents. “How do I know it is always going to obey all my rules and regulations?” he said. “This is a real concern.” He added that companies can keep the creativity of AI models by pairing them with separate systems that check a model’s work against the company’s rules and catch violations.Sivasubramanian said that one of the least appreciated parts of making AI agents work is getting them the right company data for the task. He pointed out that teams inside Amazon were showing him impressive AI agents they had built in two or three weeks. When he asked when the agents could be rolled out, he said that almost every team told him it still had to work out security, identity and monitoring.AWS in June announced a service for that purpose, called AWS Context, which maps the relationships in a company’s data for agents to use. Sivasubramanian said it’s meant to work across platforms and cloud providers, and he expects this kind of service to be a basic building block for the next 20 years, as cloud storage and databases were two decades ago.McKinsey senior partner Lari Hamalainen reportedly said that about 40% of companies claim AI has increased their profits, but only 6% describe the increase as substantial. Even as AI becomes more and more capable, there’s still lots of work to do to close the gap between “the goals, the capabilities, and what we all are aspiring to do,” McIlwain said.Madrona’s closing slide at the Summit said that returns on AI are still early for most of the companies using it but look inevitable based on what the earliest adopters are seeing.
Article Summary: Ai has boosted profits, but the jump is not substantial, according to a report by geekwire. Most ceos and ctos worry about whether an ai agent will always follow their company’s rules and regulations. Amazon web services' swami sivasubramanian said that nearly every cio and ceo raises the same question.

Article Title: In 2009, Google's Eric Schmidt and wife Wendy bought a former fisheries ship; by 2022, the vessel offered free research access and had mapped over 1.3 million square kilometres of seafloor
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt donated to Italy's National Research Council

Hosted more than 1,000 scientists

The mission continues with a bigger ship

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt transformed a former fisheries protection vessel into a philanthropic ocean research platform that, by 2022, had hosted more than 1,000 scientists and mapped over 1.3 million square kilometres of the ocean floor. According to Schmidt Ocean Institute, the vessel, named Falkor, was originally built in 1981 as a fishery protection ship. It was acquired by the Schmidts in 2009 when they founded the Schmidt Ocean Institute, an organisation focused on advancing oceanographic research and exploration. After undergoing an extensive two-year refit, Falkor was converted into what the institute described as the world's first year-round philanthropic research vessel made available to scientists at no cost.Rather than retiring the vessel, Schmidt Ocean Institute donated Falkor to Italy's Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR), the country's largest research organization, comprising 88 institutes nationwide and a marine science community of more than 450 researchers. Under CNR, the ship was renamed Gaia Blu and continues operating in the Mediterranean and beyond.Wendy Schmidt, co-founder of Schmidt Ocean Institute, said that after a decade of remarkable discoveries and scientific research, she and Eric couldn't imagine a better home for Falkor than CNR, expressing confidence that the agency would continue the ship's legacy of ocean exploration, supporting marine science, and bringing the wonders of the ocean to the public.Eric Schmidt echoed that sentiment, pointing to CNR's century of scientific experience and its track record of investing in talented researchers as reasons he believed the organization was an excellent new home for the vessel, adding that he looked forward to seeing what further discoveries would emerge from Falkor's continued work at sea.CNR president Prof. Maria Chiara Carrozza called the donation extremely beneficial for both CNR and the wider Italian scientific community, noting that it would help foster collaboration with international research institutes and universities studying the Mediterranean basin — one of the cradles of human civilization, and a region heavily impacted by human activity. She added that the vessel would give Italian scientists a unique opportunity to pursue multi-year ocean research as part of both European and other international projects.According to the institute, Falkor completed 81 research expeditions and hosted 1,056 international scientists during its time in service. The ship travelled a distance equivalent to more than 12 trips around the world while supporting marine research projects across multiple oceans.The vessel's explorations contributed to several notable discoveries, including a 500-metre-tall coral reef in Australia's Great Barrier Reef, deep-sea coral "gardens" off Western Australia, and rare footage of the elusive glass octopus.Schmidt Ocean Institute didn't step back from ocean research after donating Falkor — instead, it transitioned to an even larger vessel, Falkor (too), which launched in early fall 2022 after being outfitted with what the organization described as some of the most sophisticated maritime technology available. At 110 metres, the new ship is significantly larger than its predecessor, and has continued the Institute's core mission: operating the world's only year-round philanthropic research vessel made available to the international scientific community entirely free of cost.
Article Summary: Eric schmidt and wendy schmidt donated to italy's national research council (cnr) the vessel, named falkor, was originally built in 1981 as a fishery protection ship. It was acquired by the schmidts in 2009 when they founded the schmidt ocean institute. Under cnr, the ship was renamed gaia blu and continues operating in the mediterranean and beyond.

Article Title: India’s First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad
Article Text: KLH Hyderabad today inaugurated its Agentic AI Campus initiative and signed an MoU with HCL Group AI Labs, unveiling a roadmap that places AI-powered learning and student innovation at the centre of its academic vision. The collaboration aims to equip students across disciplines to understand, build and apply intelligent technologies through practical projects, faculty mentorship and industry engagement. Mr. Deepak Sarvanan, National Head, HCL Group AI Labs, formally inaugurated the initiative at a press meet in KLH Bachupally campus in Hyderabad.Dr. L. Koteswara Rao, Principal, KLH Bachupally, represented KLH at the MoU exchange, alongside Dr. A. Srinath, Dean – Skill Development, in the presence of other senior officials, deans, faculty and staff.The initiative aims to make AI an integral part of the student experience. From exploring concepts in the classroom to developing applications, students will be encouraged to use AI to investigate problems, test ideas and create solutions relevant to industry and society.Er. Koneru Lakshman Havish, Vice President, KL Deemed to be University said, “We want students to develop the confidence and skills to shape how AI is used in their chosen fields.Our collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs will help connect classroom learning with hands-on projects and industry expertise, giving students opportunities to build intelligent solutions for real-world needs. As we develop our Agentic AI Campus, our focus is on preparing young people to innovate responsibly and contribute meaningfully to an evolving workplace. ”Agentic AI brings a new dimension to this approach. These systems can plan and carry out a series of tasks towards a defined goal, with appropriate human oversight. Understanding how such systems work will help students explore applications that extend from analysing information to coordinating workflows and supporting decisions.The proposed roadmap envisages project-based learning in areas such as business automation, data-driven services and discipline-specific AI applications. Students will be encouraged to design and test solutions, evaluating their accuracy, reliability and practical value.Faculty readiness will be a key part of the campus’s development. The collaboration envisages supporting educators in integrating AI into teaching, assignments and mentorship, helping students connect technical understanding with critical thinking and independent judgement.Responsible AI use will remain central to the learning approach, with attention to data privacy, bias, reliability and human accountability. Students will be encouraged to question outputs, verify information and understand the limitations of the systems they develop and use.Through its collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs, KLH Hyderabad aims to strengthen the connection between academic learning and the evolving workplace across its Bachupally and Aziznagar campuses, preparing students to develop AI solutions and apply them thoughtfully to real-world challenges.
Article Summary: Klh hyderabad has signed an mou with hcl group ai labs. The collaboration aims to equip students across disciplines to understand, build and apply intelligent technologies. The initiative aims to make ai an integral part of the student experience.

Article Title: OpenAI to watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in Europe, here's what it means for users
Article Text:
What is changing

How the watermark works

Limits of detection

What it means for users

Who gets the detector

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has announced that it will add invisible watermarks to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex for users in the European Union, as the company moves to comply with new requirements under the EU AI Act. The company also said that the rollout will being over the coming weeks and will apply to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text outputs across all plans in the EU. The move is designed to make AI-generated text identifiable in a machine-readable way while promoting greater transparency around AI-created content.OpenAI said that over the coming weeks it will add the watermark to eligible text output from ChatGPT and Codex. The change covers all plans in the EU and nowhere else. The company said it is not making text watermarking a global default at launch and described the regional approach as a way to learn from real-world use and feedback.The company is also making watermarking available to developers. Starting immediately, API customers worldwide can opt in to watermarked text for select models. It stays off by default in the API. OpenAI said it is working with cloud partners to offer watermarking for its models through their services in the coming weeks.OpenAI's technology, called textGrain, adds a statistical signal to the model's word choices. Readers cannot see it. A detector looks for that pattern to judge whether a passage carries an OpenAI watermark. OpenAI has published a technical report on the method and said it plans to release the technology as open source.The company said textGrain matched or beat the other approaches it tested, including SynthID for text. It added that strong results under ideal conditions do not guarantee reliable detection in everyday use.OpenAI's own evaluations show where the technology struggles:* Length matters. At a 1% false positive rate, the detector found watermarks in about 80% of 200-token passages and about 95% of 400-token passages in content such as psychology. Detection was substantially lower for content such as mathematics, where there is less flexibility in word choice.* Editing weakens the signal. In tests on 400-token passages, swapping 10% of words for synonyms cut detection from about 92% to 66%. Swapping 25% cut it to 17%.What a watermark does and does not showOpenAI listed several things a detection result cannot tell anyone:* It does not measure how much a human contributed to the text.* It does not establish who owns the text or who is responsible for it.* It does not identify the user. It does not link the text to a person, account, prompt or conversation.* It does not verify whether the text is accurate.* The absence of a watermark does not prove a human wrote the text. Short, edited or translated text may evade detection. Text may also come from an unsupported model, predate watermarking or come from another company's tools.For people using ChatGPT or Codex in the EU, the visible experience should not change, since the marker cannot be seen. OpenAI said it found no meaningful quality difference in tests of its latest frontier model, Astra, with and without watermarking. On eight benchmarks, the scores were close, with the watermarked version slightly ahead on some and slightly behind on others.Users should understand that a watermark is not a verdict on authorship. Because it can be weakened by editing and does not identify users, it is not a reliable way to prove who wrote a passage. That matters for anyone who might otherwise treat a detection result as proof, such as teachers, employers and publishers.OpenAI said the detector does not reveal users' prompts or conversations.OpenAI is not releasing the text detector to the public. Researchers and expert organizations can apply for access, which will be granted case by case under the EU's Code of Practice on AI-generated content. The company said the risk of missed watermarks and false positives is the reason it is holding back a public release.Its tools for images and audio remain publicly available. These include a web verification tool at openai.com/verify and a Content Provenance API.
Article Summary: Chatgpt-maker openai will add invisible watermarks to text generated by chatgpt and codex for users in the european union. The move is designed to make ai-generated text identifiable in a machine-readable way while promoting greater transparency around ai-created content.

Article Title: How Intel Core Ultra processors lead in performance where Qualcomm ‘struggles’
Article Text:
Software and enterprise compatibility

Performance in real-world workloads and gaming

Meanwhile, Snapdragon uses ARM architecture to maximise battery life and efficiency at the expense of gaming performance.

Moreover, Snapdragon delivers Copilot+ AI experiences – the major difference is that Intel brings those AI experiences to the full Windows ecosystem – with native compatibility for the applications, peripherals, management tools, and developer workflows that businesses and creators already rely on.

Intel-exclusive technologies

We grew up with “Intel Inside” stickers on our PCs, a branding that made an invisible component a household symbol of trust and raw performance. Yet recent years brought turbulence, with rivals like Qualcomm squeezing Intel’s core market. Today, under the leadership of Lip-Bu Tan, the turnaround seems real. Backed by Washington and crucial partnerships with titans like Nvidia, Intel is regaining its operational stride. The legacy chipmaker launched the Core Ultra Series 3 processors (codenamed Panther Lake) at this year’s CES as Intel's first mobile platform built on the advanced Intel 18A process node – its biggest process innovation – making a strong case for its Core Ultra Series 3 processors in the AI PC race.Given the data in the public domain, the company’s chips hold a clear advantage over its competitors like Qualcomm’s Snapdragon platform – which compete in the same domain – in three areas: software and enterprise compatibility, real-world workloads like gaming and technologies that only Intel offers. Here is what Intel offers.Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors are built on the x86 architecture. This essentially means the full Windows and Chrome OS software ecosystem runs natively on them, with no emulation and no workarounds.For businesses, Intel says this brings native compatibility with decades-old business applications or software, established security agents and enterprise management tools. It also covers the range of peripheral devices that organisations already use.Intel vPro adds another layer on top. According to the company, it gives IT teams a hardware-based way to remotely manage, secure and support devices across large fleets. This includes out-of-band management that works independently of the operating system. Intel describes it as a capability built and tested over years of enterprise use, and one of its strongest selling points for corporate PC buyers.Intel also points to its AI PC platform, which it says supports more than 500 optimised AI models. The company says over 100 independent software vendors (ISVs) are engaged in optimising software for AI PCs.On the performance side, Intel says Core Ultra Series 3 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI compute. This comes from the CPU, GPU and NPU working together. The company explains that this mixed design sends each AI workload to the most efficient processing engine for the job, instead of depending on one type of processor. In practice, Intel says this keeps performance steady when several tasks run at once, such as content creation, AI inferencing, video calls and background processes.Gaming is another area Intel highlights. Its x86 architecture works with the full Windows gaming ecosystem. That includes anti-cheat software, older titles, specialised controllers and peripheral drivers. Intel says these are areas where mobile-first architectures still face compatibility gaps.Intel also has a few technologies that set its platform apart.Integration of these standards delivers up to 120 Gbps of bandwidth. It supports fast data transfer, daisy-chained displays and universal docking. Intel says this is supported natively across its platforms but is not available on mobile-first architectures.This enables hardware-accelerated video encoding and decoding directly on the processor. Intel says content creators working with high-resolution footage get faster export times, without the CPU load that software encoding demands.
Article Summary: Intel core ultra series 3 processors are built on the x86 architecture. This essentially means the full windows and chrome os software ecosystem runs natively on them, with no emulation and no workarounds. Article Title: Meet Ben Hogan, former bike mechanic turning discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs; shares free instructions online to help others recreate the design locally
Article Text: A Michigan man has been turning discarded bicycles into prosthetic legs while also teaching others how to make them, all for free. Ben Hogan, a former bike mechanic and prosthetist at Mary Free Bed Rehabilitation Hospital, founded Project Bike Leg , an initiative that makes prosthetics sourced almost entirely from repurposed bike parts. He hopes his low-cost design can eventually help millions of amputees around the world, according to a report by PEOPLE's Toria Sheffield.Hogan worked at the Michigan State University Bikes Service Centre as a student 20 years ago, where he learned to repair bikes. Bike shop general manager Tim Potter trained Hogan. “When I think about it, you know, I mean, it sometimes will tear you up,” said Potter.Hogan revealed that it all began with a random encounter. “I had a chance encounter with an amputee that walked into a bike shop I was working at in Los Angeles in 2011,” he said to the outlet. “He showed me his prosthesis unprompted, and it really informed me of how much a bike and a prosthesis had in common.” “After [later] shadowing some prosthetists at UCLA, I made the connection that it was my calling,” he added.Moreover, he shared that his desire to create something both functional and cost-efficient only grew after he learned how many amputees worldwide do not have access to the prosthetics they need.Citing World Health Organisation estimates, Hogan said that a "staggering 85-90% of amputees worldwide lack access to a proper prosthesis." “As a former bike mechanic turned prosthetist, I was naturally drawn to take a bicycle and turn it into a prosthesis,” he said. “A bike, after all, is a tool used to enhance human locomotion. The inherent design would allow for an adjustable, lightweight, structurally sound and functional prosthesis.”After seriously working and experimenting with the designs, Hogan crafted his first below-the-knee prosthesis model within a few weeks in 2013. However, he said he decided to put the project aside until he had developed his skillset more fully. “Due to the fact that I had not yet achieved a master's vantage point of the prosthetic arts, I decided to set the bike leg down until I could say that I honestly had the advanced prosthetic skillset to ‘reinvent the wheel’ of prosthetic care,” he explained.It was in the summer of 2024 that he decided he was finally ready to return to the initiative, at which point he officially founded Project Bike Leg. “I had been working at Mary Free Bed Rehabilitation Hospital for the past 8 years and had a patient who was up for the challenge. Using all of the rudimentary concepts of prosthetics that I had come to know in the previous decade, I crafted a new design of a BK [below-the-knee] bike leg that had an enhanced level of adjustability and functionality compared to the previous model. ”Andy Leedom, who lost his leg five years ago in a car accident, is one of Hogan’s bike-leg testers. Leedom is on his third prosthesis, which cost nearly $70,000. “I call myself the guinea pig,” Leedom said. “Ben’s been to enough places that he knows what is needed.”He went on to design an above-the-knee model in 2025 and decided he felt ready to share his designs on a larger scale. The prosthetic is made from over 95% bicycle parts. The foot is formed from a bike seat, strips of wheel and tyre treads, held together with spokes. The seat post and frame add stability. “If you look at the back of the knee, there are two chains,” Hogan said. “These hold the knee stable and there are two of them. ”The cable used to shift gears runs around the bike-leg to hold it together. The socket is made of wicker, which local communities could make out of material they have access to. “It’s actually a perfect application for a prosthesis, because it’s already built to take the weight of a human, so all I’ve done is reconfigure it in a different way to be a prosthesis,” Hogan said.He soon met with a physician in Ghana, where he eventually travelled to personally teach prosthetics students how to recreate his designs. He shared that by the end of his nine-day trip he and the students had successfully completed their work on building two fully-made prosthetics and given two amputees the ability to walk again. “And now they can train others in the Ghana region on how to make bike legs,” Hogan said.“This was a phenomenal experience that I will never forget, and I cannot wait to see what the local clinicians might do with the bike legs moving forward,” he said of the experience.Moreover, he is training thousands more across the globe on how to make their own prosthetic legs with the help of his website. He shares instructional videos on how to make both above-the-knee and below-the-knee bike leg prosthetics, with pages of pictures and step-by-step instructions.In a recent conversation with InvestigateTV about the project, Hogan said he has no intention to patent the design or personally profit from it. “I don’t have any intention of financially benefiting from it or patenting these designs,” he told the outlet. “I want them to be available to all parties all over the world.”For Hogan, the next step is a pilot study with amputees in third-world countries wearing bike legs full time. He hopes his invention will eventually help some of the 30 to 40 million people worldwide who need prosthetic legs.“As my sister said, your career should be your greatest gift to the world,” he said, “and I do think this is my greatest gift to the world.”
Article Summary: Ben hogan, a former bike mechanic and prosthetist at mary free bed rehabilitation hospital, founded project bike leg. He hopes his low-cost design can eventually help millions of amputees around the world. The prosthetic is made from over 95% bicycle parts.

Article Title: China tests 800-passenger flying-wing aircraft model with 85-metre span, showing how new aerodynamics could improve range and efficiency
Article Text:
PC: South China Morning Post

How large is China’s 800-passenger flying-wing aircraft

Who developed China’s 800-passenger flying-wing aircraft

What did wind tunnel tests reveal about the aircraft

A Chinese research team has unveiled an aerodynamic model for a flying-wing passenger aircraft that could carry more than 800 people, according to the South China Morning Post. The design is 85 metres wide and 43 metres long, with a wingspan roughly 1.6 times that of the B-2 Spirit stealth bomber. The Airbus A380, the world's largest passenger jet, typically seats about 555. The concept comes from the China Aerodynamics Research and Development Centre. No full-scale aircraft has been built, but a 1:52 stainless steel model was tested in a transonic wind tunnel at speeds between Mach 0.4 and 0.8.According to the South China Morning Post, the proposed design is 85 metres (280 feet) wide and 43 metres long, with a wingspan roughly 1.6 times that of the B-2 Spirit. For comparison on capacity, the report states that the Airbus A380, currently the world's largest passenger jet, typically seats about 555 passengers. The SCMP describes the Chinese design as seating more than the A380, at more than 800 passengers.According to the report, the final design has a reference wing area of about 1,395 square metres (15,015 square feet). The leading edge is swept at 37 degrees and the trailing edge at 28 degrees.The cruise speed is Mach 0.8.The concept comes from the China Aerodynamics Research and Development Centre (CARDC), a national institute that has contributed to major aircraft projects including the C919 narrowbody airliner and the Y-20 transport plane. Details were published in June in the Chinese-language Journal of Aerospace Power. According to the report, the design serves as a standard model for verifying wind tunnels, computational methods and testing equipment for long, slender flying-wing shapes.The report states that the researchers originally developed the layout for a 250-seat aircraft, similar in capacity to long-range widebody jets such as the Airbus A330 and Boeing 767. They have since scaled it up to the 800-passenger class as part of a broader push for large twin-aisle widebody airliners that began during China's 13th five-year plan, covering 2016 to 2020. The SCMP quotes aerodynamics scientist Li Yonghong and his team as writing that the high-aspect-ratio flying wing has remarkable aerodynamic advantages. They said its high lift-to-drag ratio and low induced drag could deliver longer range and lower energy consumption.A full-scale aircraft has not been built. The team is instead advancing prototype testing with a 1:52 stainless steel scale model, which measures about 0.8 metres in length and has a wingspan of 1.6 metres. The model was tested in CARDC's 2.4-metre transonic wind tunnel at speeds between Mach 0.4 and 0.8. The researchers examined aerodynamic characteristics, boundary-layer transition, measurement accuracy, lateral and longitudinal stability, and structural deformation.According to the report, the model achieved a maximum lift-to-drag ratio of about 20 at speeds below Mach 0.7, dropping to 17.6 at Mach 0.8. The team wrote that "the results confirm its excellent aerodynamic performance", qualifying it as a benchmark model for such configurations. The researchers added that the model could support studies of flow mechanisms and aeroelasticity, as well as the development of new wind tunnel testing techniques. The tests were therefore focused on validating the flying-wing configuration’s aerodynamic behaviour rather than demonstrating the performance of a completed passenger aircraft. The results provide experimental data that researchers can use when refining the design and evaluating future flying-wing concepts. China is also pressing ahead with the C929, a 280-seat long-range widebody jet expected to make its first flight around 2030, and the C949 supersonic airliner, which the report says draws parallels with Nasa's X-59 supersonic technology.
